podcast.title: Formed by Ex-Slipknot Roadies
podcast.body: The band Knives was formed by three individuals who previously worked as gear movers for the renowned metal band Slipknot, illustrating a common trajectory for roadies to create their own musical projects. "There's a band called Knives featuring three guys who used to move gear for slipknot."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: We Are The Road Crew - A History of Roadies

xref.title: Johnny Rotten's Attacks – June 1977
xref.body: Around the time "Pretty Vacant" was released, Johnny Rotten was attacked by monarchist hooligans armed with knives outside a pub called The Pegasus. His left arm was severely cut, damaging tendons to the extent that he was permanently unable to play the guitar properly. He was fortunate that his heavy leather pants deflected a blade from penetrating his thigh. Three days later, he was attacked again. "They cut up his left arm so badly that some tendons were ruined. He's never been able to play the guitar properly as a result."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Infamous Stage Antics - Self-Mutilation
xref.body: During performances, Iggy Pop would smear his body with peanut butter and raw meat, carve his chest with broken beer bottles or steak knives, resulting in "long, bleeding open wounds." He also had The Stooges guitarist Rob Ashton whip him with a real leather bullwhip and would smash himself in the head with a microphone. "He'd smear his body with peanut butter and raw meat. He'd carve up his chest using a broken beer bottle or maybe mutilate himself with a steak knife, drawing long, bleeding open wounds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About Iggy Pop

xref.title: Jack the Ripper Persona
xref.body: When performing live, he often dressed as Jack the Ripper, emerging from a coffin with knives, daggers, skulls, and fake bodies as part of his "shock horror" act. "When he performed live, he often dressed as Jack the Ripper, rising out of a coffin with his knives, daggers and skulls and fake bodies, so shock horror."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
